2026-11-29.alt: The new liturgical year begins with the season of Annunciation–Nativity (Suvara–Yalda). In the Holy Qurbana the second Anaphora (Qudasha of Mar Theodore) is used from today until Palm Sunday. The 25 Days' Fast before Christmas begins (traditionally from 1 December; check your eparchy).
2026-11-29.verse: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.”
theo: A new liturgical year begins, and the Syro-Malabar Church begins it not with the end of the world but with an announcement: good news is coming. The season of Suvara (Annunciation) leads us through the great announcements of salvation, to Zechariah, to Mary, to Joseph, until the Nativity of the Lord.

The first announcement is made to old people who had given up hope. Abraham is ninety-nine and Sarah ninety; Abraham falls on his face and laughs: “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?” Centuries later Zechariah and Elizabeth are “righteous before God”, yet childless and “getting on in years”. In both stories God does the impossible and gives a son through whom the whole plan of salvation moves forward.

Zechariah is a priest serving in the Temple. As he offers incense, the angel Gabriel says: “Do not be afraid… your prayer has been heard.” Perhaps Zechariah had long stopped praying for a child; God had not stopped listening. His son John will go before the Lord “to turn the hearts of parents to their children… to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.” The preparation for Christ begins in a family.

That is why the Epistle speaks of the family: “Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.” Husbands, wives, children and parents are the first place where salvation is lived. Isaiah's words are spoken over each family at the start of this year: “Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.”
conn: The births of Isaac and John follow the same pattern: an aged, barren couple, a divine promise, human doubt (Abraham laughs, Zechariah questions), and the gift of a son. Luke deliberately echoes Genesis to show that the God of Abraham is acting again.

Gabriel's words about John (Luke 1:17) quote Malachi 4:5–6, the last words of the Old Testament prophets: Elijah will come and turn the hearts of parents to their children. The Gospel begins where the Old Testament ended.
Zechariah receives the announcement at the hour of incense, when the people pray outside (Luke 1:10). Psalm 141:2: “Let my prayer be counted as incense before you.” The Gospel begins in the liturgy.

The angel who appears to Zechariah is the same who explained the seventy weeks to Daniel “at the time of the evening sacrifice” (Daniel 9:21). Gabriel's coming signals that the long-awaited time is fulfilled.
altar: The Gospel opens in the sanctuary, with a priest at the altar of incense. In our Qurbana, too, incense rises and the priest prays for the people. From today we use the Anaphora of Mar Theodore, one of the three ancient anaphoras of the East Syriac tradition. As Zechariah received the good news at the altar, so do we: the Word who was announced comes to us in the Mysteries.
outline: Ask: what prayer have you stopped praying because you lost hope?

2026-11-29.prayer: Lord God, faithful to your promises, at the beginning of this new year you speak to us as to Zechariah: “Do not be afraid; your prayer has been heard.” Renew our hope, bless our families, and prepare our hearts to welcome your Son. Amen.

illus: A couple in a Kerala parish prayed for a child for fourteen years. When their daughter was finally born, they named her after Elizabeth. “We had almost stopped praying,” the mother said, “but God had not stopped listening.”

family.explain: An angel told old Zechariah that he and Elizabeth would have a baby named John. God hears our prayers even when we wait a long time. John came to get people ready for Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for couples waiting for a child, and for all our families this Christmas season.
family.ask: Ask: “How will our family get ready for Jesus this year?”

catechism: The preparations for Christ's coming; John the Baptist.
The Christian family, a domestic church.
kidsaint: An old priest who served God faithfully in the Temple. When an angel brought him good news, he doubted and became mute; when John was born, he burst into a song of praise. Lesson: trust God, even when his promises seem too good to be true.
term: Syriac for “announcement” (good news). The first season of the Syro-Malabar liturgical year, recalling the announcements of the births of John and Jesus, leading to Christmas (Yalda, “birth”).

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a new liturgical year begins today. Our Church does not begin with a warning but with good news: an announcement. For four weeks we will listen to the angel's messages to Zechariah, to Mary and to Joseph, and prepare for the birth of the Lord.

The first two announcements are made to old people. Abraham is almost a hundred and Sarah ninety; when God promises a son, Abraham falls on his face and laughs. Centuries later Zechariah and Elizabeth are righteous, faithful, and childless, and they are old. Humanly, the story was over. But God is the God of the impossible.

Zechariah is offering incense in the Temple when the angel says: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, your prayer has been heard.” Perhaps he had stopped praying for a child long ago. God had not stopped listening. Is there a prayer you have stopped praying? This season is the time to take it up again.

And notice where salvation begins: in a family. John will turn the hearts of parents to their children. That is why St Paul speaks today of husbands and wives, parents and children: “Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.” Christ comes into the world through families.

So let us begin this year with hope. Let us keep the 25 Days' Fast as families, pray together, forgive one another, and make our homes ready for Jesus. God says to each of us what he said through Isaiah: “Do not fear; I have called you by name, you are mine.” Amen.
kids: Children, a new Church year starts today! It's like New Year's Day for the Church!
An angel told old Zechariah that he would have a baby boy called John. Zechariah couldn't believe it, so he couldn't speak until John was born!
God always keeps his promises. This season, let's get our hearts ready for baby Jesus. Say together: “Jesus, I'm getting ready for you!”
